classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the arc replaces a chord in the rectangle boundary and calculate both before adjusting perimeter.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows a shape $APQBCD$. The shape consists of a rectangle $ABCD$ with an arc $PQ$ on side $AB$ and with side lengths $BC=3.6\mathrm{\ m}$ and $CD=8.0\mathrm{\ m}$.

The arc $PQ$ is an arc of a circle with centre $O$ and radius $2.1\mathrm{\ m}$ and $\angle POQ=110^\circ$

What is the perimeter of the shape $APQBCD$?

Give your answer correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Rectangle ABCD with A and B above D and C. P and Q divide the upper side in order A–P–Q–B. A minor circular arc bulges above PQ. PQ, OP and OQ are dashed; O is marked below the chord. The upward central angle carries 110° without an added visible angle arc. OQ has a sloping 2.1 m label below the radius. BC and CD carry external 3.6 m and 8.0 m labels.
spec.mathematics: BC=3.6 m; CD=8.0 m; OP=OQ=2.1 m; angle POQ=110 degrees. Boundary follows AP, minor arc PQ, QB, BC, CD, DA. Construction chord PQ is excluded from the perimeter.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}PQ^2&=2.1^2+2.1^2-2(2.1)(2.1)\cos110^\circ\\[8pt]PQ&=\sqrt{2.1^2+2.1^2-2(2.1)(2.1)\cos110^\circ}\\[8pt]\ell_{\text{arc }PQ}&=\frac{110}{360}\times2\pi(2.1)\end{align*}$$
Replace chord $PQ$ in the rectangle's perimeter with arc $PQ$.
$$\begin{align*}P&=2(8.0+3.6)-\sqrt{2.1^2+2.1^2-2(2.1)(2.1)\cos110^\circ}+\frac{110}{360}\times2\pi(2.1)\\[8pt]P&\approx23.8\mathrm{\ m}\end{align*}$$
